title: CRASH-074: array walk byref userdata shared zval ptr slot separation uaf (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at Zend/zend_execute_API.c:389 in _zval_ptr_dtor when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 37d7df72a62e, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/array.c:1061 (the unconditional `zval_ptr_dtor(&key);`, with `zval *key;` uninitialised at :997 and MAKE_STD_ZVAL(key) only at :1024). Claimed line :1005 (`args[2] = userdata;`) does exist but is not what faults.
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has _zval_ptr_dtor at Zend/zend_execute_API.c:389 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #0); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
